source_refs.note: Topic 1.7.7, printed pages 13-14: the trends in electronegativity with the values of Figure 1.8 and the summary of Figure 1.9.

blocks.text: Moving from left to right along a period, electronegativity increases, because the nuclear charge increases and the size decreases. In a group it decreases from top to bottom, because the size increases with the addition of shells and the shielding effect grows. In the halogen group, for example, the value falls from fluorine (4.0) to iodine (2.5). Metals, on the left side of the table, have lower electronegativity values than non-metals, so metals are electropositive and non-metals electronegative, relatively. Figure 1.9 of the text summarises all the variation trends of the physical properties of the elements in the periodic table.

blocks.prompt: Using the printed values, state which bond is more polar, H to Cl or H to Br, and which element of period 3 is the most electropositive.
blocks.explanation: H to Cl is more polar: the difference between chlorine (3.0) and hydrogen (2.1) is 0.9, against 0.7 for bromine (2.8). Sodium (0.9) has the lowest value in period 3 and is its most electropositive element.

items: Electronegativity rises across a period (more nuclear charge, smaller atom) and falls down a group (more shells, more shielding): F 4.0 to I 2.5.
Metals on the left are electropositive, non-metals on the right electronegative.
